contexts.text: By the Philistines are represented those who take up false principles, and reason thence concerning spiritual things, which inundate man, as they did the Antediluvians.
From whom went forth the Philistines () = a nation thence, by (which) is signified the knowledge of the Knowledges of faith and charity.

In the Ancient Church all were called Philistines who spoke much concerning faith, and said that salvation is in faith, and yet had no life of faith. Therefore they were called the uncircumcised, that is, without charity. Illustrated, Explained. AC 3024:3.
Such are everywhere signified by the Philistines in the propheticals of the Word, and also in the historicals. Illustrated.
As by the Philistines were signified the Knowledges of faith, Abraham... sojourned there ... and likewise Isaac...
That the Philistine... in general, the knowledge of the Knowledges of faith; and, in special, those who place faith and salvation in Knowledges alone. Illustrated.

(The Philistines) do not reason from natural knowledges concerning spiritual and celestial thing... but they learn the Knowledges of faith and keep them in the memory with no other end than ... to know them ... As the Philistines are such, they cannot but pervert the Knowledges of faith by reasonings from them, and thus form for themselves false doctrine... and therefore they ... can with difficulty be regenerated, and receive charity. Explained.
The Philistines () = the knowledges of the Knowledges of faith and charity.
(Philistia a country of the Ancient Church.) AC 2385.
Tyre, Sidon, and Philistia ... Knowledges.
The Philistines ()... those in the knowledge of the Knowledges of truth, and not in charity.
By Philistia is signified the knowledge of the Knowledges of faith. AC 3410.
Abraham sojourned in the land of the Philistines many days () = that the Lord adjoined to the doctrine of faith very many things from the knowledge of human Knowledges.
The land of the Philistines, that is, Philistia = the knowledge of Knowledges.
Philistia () = the knowledge of the Knowledges of faith; or, what is the same, those in the knowledge of the same, but not in the goods of faith.
The king of the Philistines () = doctrinal things... (For) the Philistines = the knowledge of Knowledges, which is also that of doctrinal things. AC 3391.
The Philistines envied Isaac () = that those in the knowledge alone of Knowledges did not apprehend.
All the wells... the Philistines stopped up () = that those in the knowledge of Knowledges did not want to know interior truths which are from the Divine, and thus obliterated them. AC 3420.

In the Ancient Church, and afterwards, those were called Philistines who studied life but little, but doctrine much, and who in process of time even rejected the things which are of life, and acknowledged for the essential of the Church the things which are of faith, which they separated from life; consequently, who made nothing of the doctrinals of charity... and instead of them vaunted the doctrinals of faith, and placed the whole of religion in these. Further described.
These doctrinals, of love to the Lord and of charity, ... are rejected at this day... partly by those who are called Philistines, and also Egyptians.
Those in the knowledge alone of Knowledges, called Philistines... cannot but deny that there is an internal sense of the Word. Explained.

In the good of truth are they who are here represented by... the Philistines; namely, those who make faith the essential of the Church, and set it before charity. They who are such are in no other good than the good of truth. Explained.
Such are the doctrinals of those called Philistines in a good sense; that is, those who are solely in the doctrinals of faith, and as to life are in good, but in the good of truth...
By the Philistines who killed Saul, were represented those in faith separated. References. AC 9468:4.
The woman Samson took from the daughters of the Philistines = truth from non-good; thus truth obscured... For the Philistines = those in the doctrinals of faith, and not in a life according to them.
God led them not by the way of the land of the Philistines () = it was provided by the Divine that they should not pass to the truth of faith which is not from good.

In the historicals, where it treats of the wars The Philistines, between the sons of Israel and the Philistines... by the Philistines are represented those in faith separated, or with whom the knowledge of the Knowledges of faith is the principal thing, but not a life according to it; consequently those who teach and believe that faith alone saves.
In the other life constantly affect dominion, by fighting against others, and this so long as they are not yet devastated as to the knowledge of the Knowledges of faith.

As to the assaults by those who are in the truth of faith which is not from good, who are signified by the Philistines... in the other life they infest the upright, and continually assault... charity... until they have been vastated; that is, deprived of all the knowledge of the Knowledges of faith... At this day such are very numerous. (Their position, etc., in the World of Spirits.) AC 8099:2.
Pain caught hold of the inhabitants of Philistia () = despair of enlarging dominion with those who are in faith separated from good.

They are distinguished from the Egyptians in that they exclude the goods of charity, believing that man is saved by faith without them. (Their subsidiary doctrines enumerated.) These are the Philistines, and they are called the uncircumcised, from the evils of the love of self and the world, in which is their life.

To the sea of the Philistines () = extension... to the interior truths of faith... For by the land of Philistia is signified the knowledge of the interior things of faith... because the Ancient Church was there. Illustrated.
The Philistines, like all the nations of Canaan, represented both the goods and truths of the Church, and also evils and falsities...
That the Philistines = the interior truths of faith. Illustrated.
The Church was... afterwards turned into Philistia. DP 264:2.
That those who are in faith separated from charity are represented in the Word by the Philistines. General article.

The other religiosity (into which every Church degenerates), which derives its origin from the conceit of Own intelligence, is meant in the Word by Philistia. At this day... to Philistia belong those who are in faith, and not in charity. DFaith 50. Explained.
As this religiosity, which is of faith separated from charity, continually wants to invade the Church, the Philistines remained in Canaan...
As the Philistines represented those in faith separated from charity, they are called the uncircumcised, by which are meant those devoid of spiritual love, and thence in natural love alone...
That those in faith separated from charity are represented by the Philistines. Shown from the Word. DFaith 53.
Philistia, by which is meant faith separated from charity, would have profaned also the spiritual sense of the Word. Explained.
The Philistines (who captured the ark) = those in faith separated from charity...
Until... the Philistines had been separated in the Spiritual World...
The Philistines (in the spiritual sense of the Word) = faith without charity.
Philistia () = the Church separated from charity.
The Philistines () = those in the doctrine concerning faith alone.
Philistia = truth without good, or faith without charity. AE 581:8.

Those who believe that the interior sight alone of the natural man is faith, and that by this they are... saved, denying that the good of charity effects anything... are meant by the Philistines; and the congregation of them by Philistia.
The Philistines = those in faith alone, or in faith separated from charity.
The Philistines towards the sea () = those who separate faith from charity, or from good life...
The Philistines () = those who have falsified the truths and goods of the Word.
The sea of the Philistines, where Tyre and Sidon were, = the Knowledges of truth and good from the sense of the letter.

The Philistines represented and thence signified those who make nothing of the good of love and of charity, and thence nothing of the good of life, by placing everything of religion in knowledge and Knowledge... Hence it is evident why the Philistines so often fought with the sons of Israel, and that now the Philistines conquered and now the sons of Israel. The Philistines conquered when the sons of Israel had receded from the statutes and precepts... and the sons of Israel conquered when they had lived according to them. Illustrated.
Philistia = the religion concerning faith separated from charity. AE 741:2.
The Philistines, in the Word, = faith separated from love...

All the wars which the sons of Israel waged with the Philistines represented the combats of the spiritual man with the natural man, and thence also the combats of truth conjoined with good with truth separated from good...
As this religion is with all in the Churches who love to live a natural life, the Philistines were not subjugated in Canaan as were the rest of the nations...

The Philistines represented a religiosity separated from spiritual good... Hence, whenever the sons of Israel fell away from the worship of Jehovah... they were delivered to... the Philistines. Illustrated... But, when they returned to the worship of Jehovah... the Philistines were conquered. Illustrated.
Philistia = the Church, or those in the Church, who are indeed in truths from... revelation, but still are in filthy loves.
The daughters of the Philistines = the affections of falsity.
Then, from being a Church, it becomes either Babylon, or Philistia... Philistia, with those who love the world above all things.
The Philistines = those not in charity, and thence not in truths.
